tier_rationale: Withings' own support documentation states plainly that creating a Withings account is required, and its own privacy FAQ explains the scale cannot correctly recognize a user's weight on first use without a starting value entered through the app during account setup. An account mandatory at setup is a REJECT condition on the decision table regardless of how the device behaves afterward.
rejection_reason: No documented way to finish setting up a new Body Smart without installing the Withings/Health Mate app and creating a Withings account. Multiple independent setup guides (Withings' own developer documentation, and third-party reviews of the Body+/Body Comp/Body Smart line) describe the same required sequence: install app, create account, pair scale, enter your starting weight. There is no in-box or on-device path that skips account creation.
the_unplug_test: A brand-new, still-boxed Body Smart cannot be put into service at all without first connecting a phone to the internet, installing the Withings app, and creating an account — the scale needs that initial profile before it will show you a correct number. Once that one-time setup is done, day-to-day weighing does work without a live connection: the scale weighs you, shows the number on its own e-inkscreen, and a community-reported local buffer holds a couple of weeks of readings to sync later. That buffered independence is not guaranteed, though — Withings has required existing owners to accept new data-sharing terms in-app to keep using devices they already owned, so the offline grace period is a courtesy the vendor controls, not a right of the hardware.
offline_losses: initial device setup itself — cannot be completed without app + account + internet connection
sync of weight history and body-composition metrics to the Withings app/Withings+ dashboard
continued function if Withings requires re-acceptance of updated account/data-sharing terms, per user reports

repairability.notes: Sealed body with a coin-cell or AAA battery compartment (not confirmed which); no teardown checked.

sources.supports: Withings' own support FAQ: 'Why do I need to create an account? Creating an account is required, so your data can be safely kept.' Also states that indicating a starting weight in the app while creating an account is necessary so the scale can recognize the user on first use, tying core first-use function to the account-creation step.

Confirms the Body Smart's advanced features (BIA-based body composition, ECG-adjacent sensing) are configured and toggled entirely through the Withings app, corroborating that the app/account is the control plane for the device rather than an optional add-on.
FCC grant XNAWBS13, filed by Withings (grantee code XNA), covers 'WITHINGS BODY COMP, WITHINGS BODY SMART' under Part 15C: 2.4 GHz WiFi and Bluetooth LE radios, granted 2023-04-04.

r/withings community thread (357 upvotes, 150+ comments) documenting retroactive feature removal on other Withings devices in the same account/app ecosystem (BPM Connect losing sync capability, ScanWatch losing SpO2/heart features) and multiple independent commenters reporting they were locked out of using their own already-purchased Withings devices until they accepted new in-app data-sharing terms. Used to support vendor_risk, not the tier. A targeted search for independent reporting of a specific dated removal found none, so the ledger scores this 1 (alleged, not established) rather than 2.

open_questions: Exact retail price could not be confirmed via a direct fetch of a manufacturer or retailer page within budget (withings.com blocks automated fetches; Amazon/Best Buy fetches failed). Recent listings put it in the $100-140 range.

How many days of readings the scale actually buffers offline, and what exactly happens on-screen when that buffer is full and no sync has occurred, was not confirmed against a primary Withings source.
Whether the account-creation step can be satisfied with a throwaway/local-only account (no real email, no data-sharing consent) was not tested.
notes: This is the exact case the health domain brief asked to look for: a scale that cannot show you your own weight, on a device you already paid for, without first handing an account to the manufacturer. The rejection is about the mandatory account gate at setup, which is a bright-line rule on this site regardless of how well the scale behaves once that gate is past. The Reddit thread cited for vendor_risk also documents Withings requiring existing owners to re-consent to new data-sharing terms to keep using already-owned devices — record this as a vendor_ledger_proposal for data/vendors.json: vendor 'withings', suggested vendor_risk 2, incident type 'feature_removal_and_forced_reconsent', dated ~2025-11 to 2025-12, sourced to the r/withings open-letter thread (Class B) and worth a human corroborating with an independent press source (The Verge covered a related Withings data-sharing controversy around Dec 2025 per search results, not independently fetched here) before finalizing the ledger score.

changelog.change: vendor_risk lowered 2 -> 1. The score had no backing entry in data/vendors.json, and a search for independent corroboration of the community-reported feature removals found none. Withings added to the ledger at 1 (alleged but not established) with a note to recheck.

local_replacement_note: No self-hosted replacement was found for the account-creation gate itself. Once past setup, day-to-day weighing is locally buffered, but nothing replaces the mandatory initial handshake with Withings' cloud.

alternatives.why: A basic digital bathroom scale with no radio, no app, and no account of any kind — turns on when you step on it and shows the number. Gives up body-composition estimates entirely, but answers the question 'what is my weight' with nothing standing between you and the number.
